content:
# Psalms of Solomon — Psalm 17 — Disagreement Log
**Chapter:** PSO 17 | **Agents:** EMET / LOGOS / PNEUMA / SOPHIA

---

**Total disagreements:** 13

**1. 17:4**
EMET: 'thou didst swear to him about his seed forever: that his kingdom should not fail before thee.' All four agents agree this is the crucial Davidic covenant baseline for the messianic argument that follows.

**2. 17:5-6**
EMET: 'those to whom thou hadst made no promise' = the Hasmoneans, who were not of the Davidic line. All agents agree this is the referent. PNEUMA: 'those to whom you had given no promise' (same meaning).

**3. 17:7**
EMET: 'there arose against them a man alien to our race' = Pompey. All agents agree. The use of 'alien' (allotrios) is deliberate — a gentile, non-Davidic outsider punishes the non-Davidic usurpers.

**4. 17:21**
CRITICAL VERSE. EMET: 'See, O LORD, and raise up for them their king, the son of David.' All four agents agree on this exact phrasing. 'Son of David' (huion Dauid) is the explicit messianic title. 'At the time thou knowest' = eschatological timing left to God.

**5. 17:22**
EMET: 'break in pieces the unrighteous rulers.' LOGOS: 'shatter unrighteous rulers.' PNEUMA: 'shatter unrighteous rulers' (same). The king's task is political purification of Jerusalem — expelling foreign domination.

**6. 17:23**
EMET: 'he shall destroy the pride of the sinner as a potter's vessel.' All agree. Echo of Ps 2:9 ('you shall break them with a rod of iron / dash them in pieces like a potter's vessel').

**7. 17:24**
EMET: 'With a rod of iron...with the word of his mouth.' All four agree. Note the dual instrument: physical rod + spoken word. Later tradition (NT: Rev 19:15) will preserve the 'word of his mouth' element.

**8. 17:29**
EMET/LOGOS/SOPHIA: 'He shall judge peoples and nations in the wisdom of his righteousness. Selah.' PNEUMA: same, preserves 'Selah.' This is one of only a few uses of Selah outside the canonical Psalms.

**9. 17:32**
EMET: 'bringing as gifts her sons who had fainted.' LOGOS: 'who had been cast out.' PNEUMA: 'who had been cast to the winds.' The Greek dedoron is uncertain — 'cast out' or 'exhausted/faint.' EMET's 'fainted' follows an older reading.

**10. 17:34**
CRITICAL: 'their king shall be the LORD Messiah' (Christos Kyrios). EMET/LOGOS/SOPHIA: 'the LORD Messiah.' PNEUMA: 'the LORD Messiah.' All four agree. This is the clearest pre-Christian Jewish attestation of the term 'Lord Messiah' (= Christos Kyrios). Note: LXX Lk 2:11 uses same phrase.

**11. 17:35-36**
EMET: 'he will not put his trust in horse and rider and bow.' All agree. This deliberately contrasts with earthly kings (Deut 17:16-17) — the messianic king trusts God alone, not military might.

**12. 17:40**
EMET: 'God has made him powerful in the holy spirit.' LOGOS/SOPHIA: 'God has made him strong in the Holy Spirit.' PNEUMA: 'God has made him mighty in the Holy Spirit.' The pneuma hagion phrase is present in all agents.

**13. 17:46**
The doxological close names God as 'our king forever and ever,' echoing v.1. The gathering of the tribes, hasten-mercy prayer, and 'LORD our king forever' form an inclusio. All four agents preserve this structure.
